extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and Korean Intellectual Property Office examiners handling patent-term-extension (Korea)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for filing and examination of applications to register extensions of patent term based on regulatory approvals (drugs, veterinary drugs, agrochemicals) under the Korean Patent Act and related statutes. Covers eligibility, timing, required documents, calculation of the extension period, representation rules, and substantive/formal examination criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible subject matter for patent term extension
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension of the patent term shall include: ① an invention of medicines [limited to medicines produced with the new matter ... as active ingredient and obtained with approval for items] which is subject to approval for the items under Article 31(2) or (3) or 42(1) of the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act; and ② an invention of agricultural chemicals or raw materials (limited to agricultural chemicals or raw materials produced with the new matter as the active ingredient and registered for the first time) which are to be registered under Articles 8(1), 16(1), 17(1) of the Agrochemicals Control Act for purposes of embodying the patented invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These inventions are limited to ones that have not been practiced for a certain period of time to obtain the approval or registration under the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act or the Agrochemicals Control Act. Other inventions, even if not practiced before obtaining approval under other acts, shall not be subject to application for extension of the patent term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing: patent right must be valid at filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Application for registration of an extension of the patent right by approval, etc. can be filed only when the right of a patented invention is still valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent right has been invalidated, cancelled, or extinguished (e.g., due to failure of patent fee payment) the application shall not be recognized as valid. If an invalidation trial is pending, filing is allowed. If the patent was valid at filing but later invalidated/cancelled, examiner must give applicant opportunity to explain under Article 11; if not addressed, the application may be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice when multiple approved active ingredients are disclosed in one patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Where multiple approvals are made on multiple active ingredients in a single patent, an applicant can choose just one permitted ingredient and apply for a one-time extension of the patent term for that ingredient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: If active ingredients A, B, and C are disclosed and applicant obtained three separate approvals, the applicant may file for extension choosing only one of A, B or C for a one-time extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction when multiple approvals relate to the same active ingredient
rubrics_metrics.description: Where multiple approvals are made on the same active ingredient disclosed in a single patent, application for an extension can be filed on the initial approval only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: If Product Approval A (initial), Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient Approval B, and Dosage Form Change Approval C were obtained consecutively for the same ingredient, the extension application may be filed only on the initial approval A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple patents versus single approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Where multiple patents are involved in a single approval, the term of each patented invention with respect to the concerned approval can be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: For an approval D covering an active ingredient, separate patents for product, process, and use may each be extended by filing separate applications for each patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum extension period (cap) and calculation basis
rubrics_metrics.description: The term of a patent right may be extended by a period, up to five years, during which the patented invention could not have been practiced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the period elapsed after the date of registration of the patent right is considered. Any elapsed period attributable to the patent holder or applicant during the period of reviewing relevant documents of the application for approval/registration by the approval agency shall be excluded from calculation. If calculated period exceeds five years, the extension is capped at five years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible periods to include in extension calculation (drugs/veterinary/agrochemicals)
rubrics_metrics.description: The period to be considered includes (i) total length of clinical trials after obtaining approval from the Commissioner of the Korean Food and Drug Administration and the period for reviewing relevant documents at the KFDA for drugs (excluding veterinary), (ii) analogous clinical trial and review periods for veterinary drugs at the Animal, Plant and Fisheries Quarantine and Inspection Agency, and (iii) clinical trials by designated test/research institutes and review periods at the Rural Development Administration for agrochemicals or active ingredients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These enumerated periods are to be counted when calculating the 'period during which the patented invention could not have been practiced' for extension purposes; any other applicant-attributable delays at the approval agency are excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of application (Article 90(1) list)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application shall state: 1) name and domicile of applicant (or corporation name/place of business), 2) agent name/place of business (and designated patent attorney if a firm), 3) patent number and indication of claims for which the term is to be extended, 4) length of extension applied, 5) details of approval under Article 89(1), and 6) the ground for extension as prescribed by Ordinance (with substantiating materials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application must be filed to the Commissioner of the Korean Intellectual Property Office and contain all listed items; omissions can be grounds for rejection or return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing deadline for extension application
rubrics_metrics.description: An application shall be filed within three months from the date when approval, etc. is received under Article 89(1); however, no application may be filed within six months prior to the expiration date of the patent term under Article 88.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If application was filed before approval or outside the three-month window, or within the prohibited six-month pre-expiration window, examiner shall give applicant opportunity to explain under Article 11 and may return the application if not addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility (who may file)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant of the application to register patent term extension shall be limited to a holder of the patent right. Where the patent is jointly owned, the application shall be made in the names of all co-owners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the filer is not the holder, or the application is not filed in the names of all joint owners, it constitutes a ground for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents to attach and form-filling requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must attach 'a copy of the evidential document of the ground for extension' and 'a copy of the evidential document of representation' (when represented) using Annexed Form No. 30, and fill specified boxes: applicant name(s); patent number and application number; name of the invention; all claims including active pharmaceutical ingredients for which extension is sought; ground for extension details and evidential documents; number of days for the period (capped at five years); date of approval; content of approval (with evidential documents showing licensee status).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For drugs, evidential documents include clinical investigation plans, items license, evidential documents for Phase III trials conducted overseas, and agency review periods. For agrochemicals, include test application copies and registration certificates; for raw materials include test/analysis applications and registration. The claims must clearly state how they include the approved items (examples provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of filing the extension application
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application to register an extension of term has been filed, the term shall be deemed extended, provided that a decision to reject the application has not become final and conclusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application is withdrawn, invalidated, or returned before a final rejection decision, the term is deemed not to have been extended. Note on appeal: a rejection becomes final 30 days after service of certified copy if no appeal is initiated; if appealed, finality depends on outcome of appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation and scope of power of attorney
rubrics_metrics.description: Special authorization is not required for representation in filing an application to register patent term extension. The scope of representative's power is determined by the wording of the power of representation document (e.g., 'all patent-related proceedings').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If scope in the power document includes proceedings related to registration of a patent right or extension and the representative's name is on the application, subsequent proceedings can be handled by the representative. If the representative's name is not written on the application, representation may be ineffective. Abandonment of the application requires special power of representation; without it, a representative cannot abandon the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for rejection (Article 91 enumerated grounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner shall decide to reject an application for registration of patent term extension in any of the following cases: 1) approval is unnecessary for practicing the patented invention; 2) patentee or exclusive/non-exclusive registered licensee fails to obtain approval; 3) length of extension applied exceeds the period during which the invention could not be practiced; 4) applicant is not the patentee; 5) application filed in violation of Article 90(3) (joint-owner filing requirement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutory grounds drive substantive examination and notification of rejection; each ground is further elaborated in the guideline (see detailed determinations on necessity, identicalness, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination procedure and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: The procedure for examining an application to register patent term extension is similar to that for a patent application; if no special procedure exists, patent application examination procedure applies mutatis mutandis. Once received and transferred to an examiner, examination shall be initiated within four months from receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process steps: formalities examination (by receiving division or examiner), substantive Examination I (determine any ground for rejection and notify applicant), opportunity to submit written argument or amend within designated period, re-examination considering amendments/arguments, decision to register or reject; if new grounds are found, notify and repeat procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities examination treatment (late filing, representation, fees, formalities)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application is filed after the statutory period under Article 90(2), or was filed before obtaining approval, the examiner shall notify intention to return the application and give period for explanation per Article 11(2). For violations regarding representative provisions, unpaid fees, or other formalities, examiner shall order amendment within one month (extendable by one month).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If irregularities are not addressed within the designated period despite request for amendment, the examiner shall invalidate the procedure in the name of the Commissioner. If applicant requests return after notification and submitted explanation is groundless, examiner shall return documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of subject matter for examination when amendments filed
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents subject to examination include the written application and attached documents. Where amendments are made, examiner determines if an amendment is legitimate; if legitimate, the amended matters are reflected in examination; if not, amendment is treated as never filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If more than two amendments, determine amended matters based on final amendments combination. Example provided where conflicting multiple amendments result in the application reflecting only the first legitimate amendment being examined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of 'necessity for approval' (substantive test)
rubrics_metrics.description: To recognize that approval under Article 89(1) is necessary for practicing the patented invention, the following requirements shall be met: ① approval is required for practicing (e.g., manufacturing/production) of the approved substance; ② composition of the patented substance is identical with the approved substance; or ③ the use of the patented substance is identical with the approved substance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Necessity is generally recognized when the approval-granting organization has approved the concerned application; examiners may request opinions from relevant organizations if unsure. If approval is deemed not required, examiner shall notify ground for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of identicalness of composition between claimed and approved substance
rubrics_metrics.description: The approved substance must have the same composition as the substance recited in claims (for substance inventions) or as the matter manufactured by the claimed method (for method inventions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For substance inventions compare the claimed substance and approved substance directly. For manufacturing-method inventions compare the substance produced by the disclosed method with the approved substance; manufacturing methods need not be compared. If compositions are not identical, examiner shall notify a ground for rejection under Article 91(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of identicalness of use for use-inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patented subject matter is a use invention, the use of the approved substance must be the same as the use of the substance disclosed in the patent; if not, the patent term shall not be extended even if compositions are identical. If the claimed use includes the approved use, the uses are deemed the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requires comparison of claimed therapeutic/functional uses versus those in the approval. If approved use is narrower than claimed use but included within claimed use, extension may be allowed; if disparate, reject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion: intermediates, catalysts, and manufacturing devices not eligible
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent right regarding a manufacturing device for a final product and a catalyst used for manufacturing an intermediate and final product shall not be subject to extension of the patent term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acts securing safety (e.g., Pharmaceutical Affairs Act) govern manufacture and sale of final products, not intermediates. Intermediates do not require approval. Therefore, if extension is sought for an intermediate or catalyst based on approval of a final product, examiner shall notify ground for rejection under Article 91(1)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement re: patentee/licensee obtaining approval (ground for rejection if not obtained)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be rejected where the patentee, or a person who has an exclusive or registered non-exclusive license under the patent right has not obtained approval under Article 89(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guideline notes nuances (e.g., when only some of multiple patentees or licensees have obtained approval), and elaborates further beyond this chunk; examiners should apply the detailed rules in the full guideline when evaluating this ground.
